name: The Thin-File / High-Earner
description: High net income (₹1,50,000/mo), but zero credit bureau history (CIBIL = -1 / NTC). Tests lender ability to underwrite New-To-Credit applicants.

name: The Over-Leveraged Professional
description: Excellent credit score (CIBIL 780) and high salary (₹1,20,000/mo), but existing EMIs of ₹65,000 plus ₹2,00,000 credit card balance (5% load: ₹10,000) create total liabilities of ₹75,000, breaching FOIR thresholds (>60%).

name: The Credit-Impaired Applicant
description: Stable salary (₹45,000/mo) and steady job tenure, but compromised credit score (CIBIL 610) with 30 DPD and 4 inquiries knocks out banks and tier-1 NBFCs.

name: The Job Hopper
description: Joined current employer 1 month ago with 8 months total experience. Fails standard employment stability cutoffs (min 3m-6m current / 12m-24m total).

name: The Senior Near Retirement
description: Age 58 with ₹80,000 salary and CIBIL 760. Tests maximum tenure truncation because borrower will reach retirement cutoff (60 years) in 24 months.

name: The Young Fresh Graduate
description: Age 20 with ₹35,000 salary. Violates the strict minimum age limit (21 years) across traditional banks and NBFCs.

name: The Minimum Wage Salaried Worker
description: Net income ₹14,000/mo in a Metro. Falls below bank income hurdles (₹20k - ₹25k) but qualifies at inclusive fintech lenders.

name: The Gig / Contract / Self-Employed
description: Self-employed consultant earning ₹90,000/mo, CIBIL 730. Tests product suitability since standard salaried-only personal loan programs auto-reject.

name: The Top-Tier Corporate Employee
description: Prime profile: ₹2,00,000 net salary at Fortune 500 CAT-A MNC, CIBIL 820, zero debt. Qualifies for maximum salary multiplier (22x-24x) and prime rates across all 20 lenders.

name: The Boundary Case
description: Exact boundary test: Exactly 21 years old, exactly ₹25,000 income, CIBIL exactly 700, exactly 24m total and 6m current experience, 0 DPD.
